name: Winback Flow (2 Emails)
purpose: Bring back first-time customers who never ordered again, timed to the brand's real lifecycle: past the natural reorder point, before the habit is gone.

source.note: Fluid flow system v2, distilled from 31 client strategies (fluid-flow-strategist skill)

profileFilter.description: Placed Order equals 1 over all time (first-time customers)
Placed Order zero times since starting this flow

actions.job: What's new, what they bought before, and the winback code
subject: We miss you, {{first_name}}
actions.name: Email #1: We miss you
actions.sendingTo: First-time customers who have never purchased again
actions.offer: Winback code, the ceiling offer (15–25%, or $50): {{offers.winback_code}}

replenishable: What's changed since they left (new products, flavors, batches)
Reorder block with what they bought before
An easy way to tell the brand if something went wrong
one_off: New arrivals and refreshed best sellers
Recommendations based on what they bought before (dynamic)
The reason they chose the brand
Coming back should feel like a style refresh or upgrade, never a clearance event

actions.job: Same code with a clear expiry
subject: Your offer expires soon
actions.name: Email #2: Come back offer
actions.sendingTo: First-time customers who have never purchased again

all: The same code with a clear expiry
replenishable: Subscription for anyone who'd otherwise lapse again
one_off: One primary CTA to their recommended collection

variables.description: Days after first order. DATA: where ~70% of repeat orders have happened. Replenishable: past the reorder point (30-day supply → ~45 days); split by product group when cycles differ (SPQR 60/90). One-off: 60–180, 90 most often; split by segment

notes: Email #2 lands 3–7 days after #1 (replenishable) or 3–14 (one-off); 5 is the default. Liquid Surf used plain text for a check-in tone (template winback/01a-check-in-plain).
